intro: The Andaman highlight that keeps drawing people back: a single day on the water hitting multiple islands — Phi Phi, Maya Bay, James Bond Island, Phang Nga Bay. Clear water, dramatic limestone karsts. This guide picks the most-booked tours departing from Phuket (bookable in advance on Klook), explains the difference between speedboats and big boats, what national park fees to expect, and the best season to go.
chips: 🏖️ Phi Phi · Maya Bay · James Bond
quickAnswerHtml: Most Andaman island-hopping tours depart from Phuket / Khao Lak as day trips. The two flagship routes are Phi Phi + Maya Bay (from The Beach) and James Bond Island + Phang Nga Bay (limestone karsts, kayaking in caves). Choose a speedboat (faster, more stops) or a big boat (steadier, more relaxed). Prices run around 1,200–2,500 THB per person, usually including transfers and lunch. There's a separate national park fee of ~400 THB/person paid on-site. Clearest water: Nov–Apr.

blocks.html: Island hopping means one boat, multiple islands, one day — stopping to snorkel, take photos, and swim in sheltered bays. The Andaman coast (Phuket, Krabi, Phang Nga) is where this works best. The main decision is choosing your route (Phi Phi vs Phang Nga Bay) and the type of boat to match your travel style.

blocks.text: How to choose the right tour

items: Want to hit multiple stops and snorkel in clear water → Phi Phi + Maya Bay + Khai Islands route (speedboat)
Prefer dramatic limestone scenery and kayaking in caves → James Bond Island + Phang Nga Bay route
Prone to seasickness or traveling with children or elderly → choose a big boat (steadier, less rushed)
Want quiet with fewer people → take the early morning slot and avoid peak high season
Budget for a national park fee paid on-site (~400 THB/person for foreigners)

blocks.html: The Andaman coast is clearest and calmest from Nov–Apr. Monsoon season (May–Oct) brings stronger swells and some tours are cancelled. Maya Bay is open but has visitor caps and timed entry to allow coral recovery — most tours handle the logistics. The national park fee (~400 THB/person for foreigners) is usually paid separately on-site, not included in the tour price. If you want to add scuba diving, see the Thailand diving guide.

blocks.title: Get the most out of your island day

items.title: Take the early slot
items.text: Morning departures mean calmer seas, better light, and fewer people at Maya Bay. Worth the early wake-up.

items.title: Use reef-safe sunscreen
items.text: Reef-safe sunscreen, a hat, UV-protection rash guard for snorkeling — the tropical sun is strong on open water.

items.title: Seasick-prone? Go big boat
items.text: Speedboats are fast but slam through chop. If you get seasick, choose a big boat and sit midship. Bring motion-sickness tablets.

items.title: Bring cash for the park fee
items.text: Have cash ready for the national park fee (~400 THB/person) paid on-site — it's usually separate from your tour price.

faq.q: Where is the best island hopping in Thailand?
faq.a: The Andaman coast from Phuket is the top pick. Key routes: Phi Phi + Maya Bay (clear water, snorkeling) and James Bond Island + Phang Nga Bay (limestone karsts, kayaking). Krabi also runs a 4-island tour worth considering.

faq.q: What is the difference between a speedboat and a big boat?
faq.a: Speedboats are faster and can cover more stops in a day but slam through waves. Big boats are steadier and more relaxed — better for anyone prone to seasickness, families with children, or older travelers.

faq.q: How much does an island-hopping tour cost?
faq.a: Around 1,200–2,500 THB per person, usually including transfers from your hotel and lunch. The national park fee (~400 THB/person for foreigners) is typically paid separately on-site. Check exact pricing when booking.

faq.q: When is the best time to go?
faq.a: The Andaman coast is clearest and calmest Nov–Apr. During monsoon season (May–Oct) swells pick up and some tours may be cancelled.
